instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) with a rack in the middle.
Peel and devein the shrimp if they aren't already, and pull off the tails. Pat them dry, sprinkle 1/2 tsp of the salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper over them and keep them in the fridge until you need them.
Finely chop the onion. Cut the bell pepper into 1/2 inch pieces. Mince the garlic. Drain the diced tomatoes over a bowl and keep the juice.
Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a 12 inch ovenproof skillet over medium. Add the onion, bell pepper and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook, stirring now and then, for 5 to 7 minutes, until they're soft.
Stir in the 1 tbsp tomato paste and cook for about 1 minute, until it turns a shade darker. Add the garlic and the 1/2 tsp oregano and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell the garlic.
Add the 2 cups orzo and stir it for about 4 minutes, until some of it is lightly golden.

Pour in the 3 cups broth and the tomato juice, and add the last 1/4 tsp salt. Let it simmer, stirring often so the orzo doesn't stick, for 10 to 12 minutes, until the orzo is almost tender with a firm bite in the middle.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the shrimp and the drained tomatoes, then crumble 3/4 cup of the feta evenly over the top.
Transfer the pan to the oven and bake for about 20 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and the feta is lightly browned. Cut one shrimp in half to check: it's done when it's opaque all the way through.
While it bakes, chop 1/4 cup of the parsley and cut the lemon into wedges.
Take the pan out with an oven mitt. The handle will be hot.
Taste the orzo. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Scatter the parsley over the top and serve with the lemon wedges.
method_notes: All three put shrimp with orzo, tomato and feta. America's Test Kitchen (the lead) softens onion and bell pepper, toasts the orzo, simmers it in broth and the tomato juice until nearly done, then stirs in raw shrimp and diced tomatoes, tops it with feta and bakes it at 375°F; Mia Kouppa cooks the orzo in tomato sauce on the stove and fries the shrimp separately, and Food.com's Garides Youvetsi bakes shrimp under tomato sauce, feta and Parmesan with no orzo. This version follows the lead's method and amounts but leaves out its saffron, peas and scallions, adds the fried tomato paste from Mia Kouppa, and finishes with Mia Kouppa's parsley and the lead's lemon wedges. The lead's page shows its rating as a whole 4, so the decimal is unknown.
